notes: A legendary fly-in destination since the 1960s. Aviation-themed décor and homemade pies — marionberry and rhubarb are the ones to get. Named a Top 10 Airport Restaurant by AOPA. Watch planes taxi past while you eat. Wed–Sun 8AM–4PM.

Amelia Earhart-themed restaurant inside a plane hangar at Bremerton National. American classics with generous portions. Sunday brunch buffet draws pilots and locals alike. Tue–Thu 6AM–8PM · Fri–Sat 6AM–9PM · Sun 6AM–8PM · Closed Mon.
On-field restaurant right at Tacoma Narrows with runway views. Burgers, pizza, Cajun tots and Harmon craft beers on tap. Watch GA aircraft and business jets roll by. Open daily 11AM–9PM.

World-famous fly-in fishing resort on the White River. The restaurant serves fresh trout caught steps from the table. One of the most unique fly-in dining experiences in the country — land on the private strip and walk to the table.

Classic airport diner at Chino Airport — home of the Planes of Fame Air Museum. Breakfast and lunch staples served with a side of warbird sightings. A longtime favorite for pilots flying the Southern California basin.

A legendary California pit stop on the I-5 corridor. Land at the private Harris Ranch strip and walk to one of the state's most famous steakhouses. Prime beef raised on-site. Open for breakfast, lunch and dinner daily.
Popular on-field café at Camarillo Airport serving breakfast and lunch. Generous portions and a friendly pilot crowd. On clear days the Channel Islands are visible from the ramp. Open daily 7AM–3PM.

Upscale dining with panoramic views of the Front Range and runway at Centennial Airport. One of Colorado's best airport restaurants — think steaks and Colorado craft beers with a view of the Rockies. Open for lunch and dinner.

On-field restaurant at Waterbury-Oxford with runway views. Breakfast and lunch served daily. Local favorite for weekend fly-ins in the Connecticut hills. Named for the airport elevation — 726 feet MSL.
status_note: Closed under Connecticut's COVID dine-in ban and never reopened. Volo now occupies the same building at 7 Juliano Drive.

notes: Located inside the famous Spruce Creek Fly-In community — one of the largest residential airparks in the world. Casual café atmosphere with a mix of resident pilots and visiting aviators. Great spot to soak up the unique fly-in neighborhood vibe.
status_note: Sold abruptly in June 2023; the new owners reopened the space as Fly In Cafe.

notes: A Vero Beach institution right on the airport with sweeping runway views. Known for generous portions of American comfort food and a lively bar. Popular with both Piper training fleet pilots from next door and transient GA traffic.

Casual on-field diner at Winter Haven Regional serving breakfast and lunch. Friendly staff and a loyal local pilot following. Good stopping point between Tampa and Orlando in the heart of central Florida's lake country.

On-field restaurant at Bartow Municipal in the heart of Polk County. Breakfast and lunch with views of the ramp and a rotating menu of daily specials. A quiet alternative to busier central Florida airports.
status_note: Ceased operations in 2024 with no public announcement. Tantrums Flightside Cafe now runs the terminal restaurant.

notes: Relaxed café at Venice Municipal — the shark tooth capital of the world. Breakfast and lunch with a friendly airport crowd. Venice has one of the most active GA communities on Florida's Gulf Coast.

On-field café at Ocala International serving breakfast and lunch to the north-central Florida GA community. Horse country surrounds the airport — a good fuel and food stop between Gainesville and the I-4 corridor.
status_note: Closed at the old terminal on SW 60th Ave. Ocala's airport restaurant is now Elevation 89, in the newer Sheltair terminal building.

notes: Waterfront airport restaurant at Albert Whitted with stunning views of Tampa Bay and the St. Pete skyline. One of Florida's most scenic dining spots. Open for breakfast and lunch — arrive early on weekends.

Down-home Florida diner at Okeechobee County Airport. Breakfast and lunch served to a mix of ag pilots, fishermen and cross-country traffic. Okeechobee sits at the north end of the lake — good stopping point for south Florida trips.

Casual café at Fort Lauderdale Executive — one of the busiest GA airports in the country. Breakfast and lunch with a front-row seat to a parade of jets, turboprops and helicopters. Great people-watching between bites.

WWII-themed restaurant adjacent to DeKalb-Peachtree with a control tower you can dine in. Runway views, wartime memorabilia and a full menu of American classics. One of the most atmospheric airport-adjacent restaurants in the Southeast.

Beloved on-field diner at Schaumburg Regional in the Chicago suburbs. Big breakfasts, burgers and a loyal pilot crowd. One of the busiest small GA airports in Illinois — expect company on weekend mornings.

Waterfront restaurant on Eagle Creek Reservoir adjacent to Eagle Creek Airpark. Seafood, burgers and lake views. A fun combination of the boating and flying communities in one spot on the west side of Indianapolis.

Historic hotel café at a private Kansas airstrip. The Beaumont Hotel dates to 1879 and has hosted cattle drives and oil barons. A genuine step back in time — land at the grass strip and walk to the dining room.

French bistro in the historic terminal at Bowman Field — one of the oldest operating airports in the US. White tablecloths and classic French cuisine next to a ramp full of vintage aircraft. A genuinely surprising find at a Kentucky GA airport.

Classic New England airport diner at Minute Man Airfield west of Boston. Famous among local pilots for generous breakfasts and friendly service. The airfield has strong ties to the local Civil Air Patrol and EAA community.
status_note: Closed in spring 2023 when the owner retired after 27 years. Fourth & Field opened in the space that September.

notes: On-field restaurant at Nantucket Memorial with views of one of the most scenic GA airports on the East Coast. Breakfast and lunch — expect a mix of island residents, ferry commuters and summer transient traffic from throughout the Northeast.

Upscale farm-to-table dining in the historic Holman Field terminal building overlooking the Mississippi River and downtown St. Paul skyline. One of the most architecturally beautiful airport restaurants in the Midwest. Lunch and dinner.

A genuine BBQ landmark accessible only by air or a bumpy dirt road. Fly into this grass strip in the North Carolina Sandhills and taxi up to a pulled pork sandwich that's worth the trip. A bucket-list fly-in for East Coast pilots. Thu–Sun only.

On-field diner at Cape May Airport on the southern tip of New Jersey. Breakfast and lunch served to a mix of shore-bound vacationers and transient GA traffic. One of the more scenic GA airports in the mid-Atlantic.
status_note: A fire-suppression pipe burst in early February 2026 and flooded the building. Engineering reports put repairs in the millions, the lease was terminated, and the owner announced permanent closure on March 14, 2026. Note: capemayairport.com still advertises the diner as open — it is not.

notes: On-field café at Gabreski Airport on Long Island's East End — gateway to the Hamptons. Breakfast and lunch with ramp views. A popular fuel and food stop for NYC-area pilots heading out to eastern Long Island.
status_note: A new chef-owner took over in the fall of 2020 and rebranded the space as Cafe Volo.

notes: Beloved Hudson Valley airport diner at Sky Acres. Breakfast and lunch served to a tight-knit local flying community. The airport has one of the most active pilot communities in the mid-Hudson Valley. Worth the trip from NYC.

On-field restaurant at Lunken Airport — one of the oldest airports in the country — with art deco terminal views and a classic American menu. Breakfast and lunch. A beloved institution for the Cincinnati aviation community.
status_note: Closed September 20, 2020 after decades at Lunken. The terminal restaurant space has been vacant since; a boutique hotel with its own restaurant is under construction as of 2026.

notes: Named for the Ford Tri-Motor, this diner at Erie-Ottawa International sits on the shores of Lake Erie. Breakfast and lunch with lake views. Port Clinton is the walleye capital of the world — fish specials are a regular feature.

Down-home Oklahoma diner at Ardmore Municipal with a devoted local following. Breakfast and lunch at a price that makes you feel like you're back in 1985. A good fuel stop on the I-35 corridor between Oklahoma City and Dallas.

Upscale Italian steakhouse at Arnold Palmer Regional — fittingly, in the hometown of the King himself. One of the more elegant airport restaurants in the Northeast. Dinner-focused with a full bar and sweeping views of the Laurel Highlands.

On-field café at Greenville Downtown with ramp views and a loyal local pilot crowd. Breakfast and lunch in the heart of the South Carolina Upstate. The airport sits minutes from downtown Greenville — one of the most revitalized mid-size cities in the Southeast.
status_note: The Airport Commission did not renew the lease after 15 years. Hangar 28 Kitchen & Events opened in the space in July 2026.

notes: A Texas institution. The Southern Flyer is one of the most talked-about airport diners in the state — chicken fried steak, jalapeño cornbread and sweet tea. Brenham is Blue Bell ice cream country. Breakfast and lunch Fri–Sun. Worth planning a trip around.
status_note: Closed in the COVID dine-in shutdown. A successor, the Dreamliner Diner, ran Dec 2021 – Dec 2022; the space has been under renovation since.

notes: On-field café at Garner Field in the Texas Hill Country. Breakfast and lunch with a strong local ranching and hunting crowd. Uvalde is one of the highest-density quail hunting areas in Texas — expect to share the ramp with hunting camp traffic in season.

One of Texas's most celebrated BBQ joints — brisket, ribs and sausage cooked over mesquite in open pits out front. A short drive from Stephenville Clark Regional in the heart of Cowboy Country. The smell hits you a mile out. Open daily.

On-field restaurant at Hooks — one of the busiest GA airports in the Houston metro. Breakfast and lunch with ramp views of a constant stream of GA traffic. A reliable fuel-and-food stop north of Houston.

A Red River institution since 1972, built on all-you-can-eat fried catfish with homemade hushpuppies, fresh-cut fries, coleslaw and a green tomato relish, finished with fried pies. For decades the turf strip ran right up to the door and this was one of the best-known fly-in meals in the region. Thu–Fri 5PM–8PM · Sat 1PM–8PM · Sun 1PM–7PM · Closed Mon–Wed.
status_note: The restaurant is still open — the airstrip is not. T40 is listed closed and non-operational as of February 2020, and pilot reports indicate it had been shut to transient traffic for roughly a decade before that after two 2007 accidents made liability insurance untenable. The airport is literally named for the restaurant, which is why fly-in directories keep listing it. Reachable by car only.

notes: Upscale restaurant at Scottsdale Airport with sweeping desert views and a sleek modern interior. One of the most polished airport dining experiences in the Southwest. Lunch and dinner — expect a sophisticated crowd and a serious cocktail program.

Perched on top of the Sedona Airport mesa at 4,800 feet with arguably the most dramatic views of any airport restaurant in the country. Red rock formations in every direction. Breakfast and lunch — arrive early before the tour helicopter traffic picks up.

On-field restaurant established in 1968 at Salem McNary Field with windows on three sides giving panoramic views of the runway and Cascade Mountains. Northwest American cuisine with homemade soups, desserts and a full bar. A classic $100 hamburger destination on the I-5 corridor. Mon–Fri 11AM–9PM · Sat–Sun 8AM–9PM.

On-field diner at Arlington Municipal with direct runway views and a devoted local following. Classic American breakfast and lunch — the omelets and French fries draw particular praise. A lively spot with a full bar and a mix of pilots, hangar tenants and locals. Mon–Fri 8AM–2PM · Sat–Sun 8AM–2PM.

Opened in the former Restaurant 121 space, roughly 300 feet off the runway with floor-to-ceiling glass and both indoor and patio seating. Run by Executive Cuisine, a corporate in-flight catering company that moved its operation into the building in 2024 — the kitchen's aviation credentials are literal. Casual fine dining: elevated American plates plus Neapolitan pizza, with happy hour at the bar Wed–Sun 3–6PM. Open daily 11AM–9:30PM. Reservations suggested for parties of five or more.

A family-run farm-to-table restaurant that took over Nancy's Air Field Café in September 2023, with about 70 seats indoors and a 75-seat patio looking out over the field. The kitchen sources from named local farms and twenty of its own garden beds; brunch is the move — corned beef hash, build-your-own omelettes, steak and cheese on an everything bagel. Wed–Fri lunch 11AM–3PM and dinner from 4PM · Sat brunch 9AM–3PM and dinner from 4PM · Sun brunch 9AM–3PM · Closed Mon–Tue. Note the field itself is on the market as of 2026, though the owners say it is business as usual.

Opened September 2023 in the old Downwind Café space, keeping the cozy aviation-themed room and leaning into it on the menu — the Fly-In Omelet, the Spruce Creek Scrambler, and pizzas named The Ranch Runway and The Margherita Maneuver. Full bar, happy hour 3–7PM, live music Fri and Sat nights. Read this before you go: despite the name, 7FL6 is a private residential airpark and the restaurant states plainly that its runway may not be used to visit. You drive in through a guarded gate with a valid license. Breakfast Tue–Sat 8–11AM, Sun 8AM–12PM · Lunch Tue–Sat 11:30AM–4PM, Sun 12–4PM · Dinner Sun and Tue–Thu 4–8PM · Closed Mon.

Took over the former Apron Cafe space in the fall of 2020, sitting at the base of the tower with a view of traffic working the field. A breakfast-and-lunch operation rather than a dinner house, with a steady local following alongside airport traffic. Hours are not posted publicly and sources disagree — call (631) 998-3573 before you launch. Unrelated to Volo at Oxford, Connecticut, despite the name.

Opened July 8, 2026 in the old Runway Café space on the South Ramp, and worth the detour if you have been missing the original. Chef-owner Trish Ballentine runs a scratch kitchen — handcrafted sandwiches, house-roasted meats, shareable plates and rotating weekly specials — with a full bar and house-made mixers. A 16-foot glass hangar door frames the runway, and there is a gated playground for anyone flying with kids. Currently Tue–Sun 11AM–3PM, closed Mon; dinner and weekend breakfast have been announced but are not yet running. The name honors two women born in 1928 and nods to the airport's 2028 centennial.

A family-run operation inside the Bartow terminal building with ramp and runway views, serving Old Florida comfort food. Breakfast runs to the Pilot's Breakfast, chicken and waffles, and shrimp and grits; lunch to the Signature Smash Burger, a Cuban, Shrimp & Grit Cakes and gator bites. Burger Monday, Taco Tuesday and a Friday fish fry rotate through the week, and there is key lime pie waiting at the end of it. Mon–Sat 7AM–2PM · Closed Sun.

The most polished restaurant on this map that still lets you park on the ramp and walk in. Opened 2021 in the center of the Sheltair terminal: floor-to-ceiling windows onto the runway, a bar built from an aircraft wing, taxi-light housings repurposed as table fixtures, and equestrian touches for Marion County horse country. Crab cakes, porcini-dusted scallops, lobster spring rolls, and a serious burger list including the Flying Goat with goat cheese and fig jam. Sun–Thu 11AM–9PM · Fri–Sat 11AM–10PM. Reservations on OpenTable; sunset over the runway is the draw.

About as short a walk as fly-in dining gets — the cafe sits on the east side of the runway, roughly 200 feet from the transient tie-downs. A straightforward family-run diner: eggs, hash browns, corned beef hash, biscuits and gravy, country fried steak, and window seats looking straight out at the pattern. Independence charges no landing or tie-down fees. Plan it as a morning flight — the kitchen closes at 2PM every day. Mon–Sat 6AM–2PM · Sun 7AM–2PM.

One of the few fly-in options in Puget Sound that will still feed you at 8PM — open seven days from 7AM for breakfast through dinner, which is unusual for an on-field restaurant. Hand-cut Angus steaks aged at least 28 days are the house specialty, with all-day breakfast, a full bar, and indoor and outdoor seating. Harvey Field is shared with skydiving and balloon operations, so brief the parachute activity and expect a busy pattern on good-weather weekends. Sun–Thu 7AM–9PM · Fri–Sat 7AM–10PM. The restaurant's lease has been extended through at least September 2027.

airport_name: City of Colorado Springs Municipal Airport
notes: You eat inside a 1953 Boeing KC-97 tanker — 42 of the roughly 275 seats are in the airframe itself, and the cockpit is open to walk through. Diner-plus American: the Reuben von Crashed, the BBQ Bomber Burger, Runway Chicken Wings, Angus steaks. It is outside the airport fence, but the walk is genuinely easy: out the landside door at Cutter Aviation or the Colorado Jet Center and southwest to Newport Road, about half a mile and ten minutes on foot, no ramp crossing and no badging. Sun–Thu 11AM–8PM · Fri–Sat 11AM–9PM.
